sections.label: Real Estate & PropTech
sections.challenge: Your listings look like everyone else's because you all use the same portal template. Buyers judge a property in seconds from imagery and a price, and judge you in the same glance. Meanwhile the software your agents use was designed for a desktop in an office, not a phone in a hallway.

sections.heading: What we fix in property businesses

cards.title: A brand that cannot carry the price
cards.body: Premium property sold through a generic identity loses the argument before the viewing. We build brands where the typography, pacing, and photography direction justify the number on the listing.

cards.title: Search that fights the buyer
cards.body: Filters built around the database rather than the decision. We design search around how people actually narrow — location feel, light, layout, commute — not only bedrooms and price.

cards.title: Agent tools designed for a desk
cards.body: The people using your platform are standing in a property with one hand free. We design for that context first, then scale the interface up to desktop.

What property teams need,

steps.label: Launch
steps.title: Establish credibility fast
steps.body: Identity, a site that makes the portfolio look worth its price, and the launch assets a new agency or development needs to be taken seriously from week one.

steps.label: Growth
steps.title: Turn traffic into enquiries
steps.body: Listing and search experiences designed around the buyer's real decision, with enquiry paths that do not ask for a phone number before showing a floor plan.

steps.label: Platform
steps.title: Software people choose to use
steps.body: Agent, landlord, and tenant tools designed for the phone, with the dense data views and permissions a maturing proptech platform needs.

cards.title: What makes a real estate website convert?
cards.body: Photography given room to work, a clear price and location above the fold, and an enquiry step that asks for the minimum. Most property sites lose people by demanding registration too early.

cards.title: Can you work with portal data feeds?
cards.body: Yes. We design around the feed you have — MLS, Rightmove, or a custom API — including the ugly realities of inconsistent image sizes and missing fields. [PLACEHOLDER: name the feeds you have integrated.]

cards.title: Do you design for developers and new builds?
cards.body: Yes: project launch sites, unit selectors, floor plan interfaces, and the brochure and collateral that go with a development launch.

cards.title: Do you handle photography and CGI?
cards.body: [PLACEHOLDER: confirm. We art-direct and specify; say here whether you produce, partner, or brief the client's own suppliers.]

cards.title: Can you build the site as well as design it?
cards.body: Yes — Webflow, Framer, or WordPress with the listing CMS modelled so your team can publish a property without a developer.

cards.title: How long does a property brand and site take?
cards.body: An identity takes four to six weeks; a listing site six to ten including build. A full platform product is scoped separately.
